title: Coping with Loneliness: Evaluation of a Mechanism-Based Psychotherapy Module
summary:
Experts estimate that about 10 to 20 percent of people in Germany feel lonely for a long time. This can seriously affect both physical and mental health. People who are lonely are more likely to become ill or develop mental health problems. These problems can also last longer. Studies have shown that lonely people are more often admitted to psychiatric hospitals. But loneliness doesn’t just happen because someone is alone. Many different things can play a role – for example, a strong fear of rejection, having few or weak social connections, or not treating oneself with care and kindness.
This is where the planned project comes in. The goal is to test a group therapy program that focuses on the causes and maintaining factors of loneliness. We want to find out if the program works well – both in hospitals and for people who are treated outside of hospitals. To learn more, participants will be asked questions at several points in time – not only about loneliness, but also about other things that may be connected to it.

interventions.name: The planned group intervention consists of 10 sessions, each lasting 90 minutes, for 6–8 participants.
